# ClaimValueCheck

> Free self-help tools for people with a Texas personal-injury claim. The tools
> help people answer two questions: how long they have to file a claim, and
> roughly what that claim could be worth. All calculations use fixed, hard-coded
> formulas based on the Texas Civil Practice & Remedies Code — not AI — and every
> result cites the governing statute. The site is attorney advertising and does
> not provide legal advice; the responsible attorney is identified in the footer.

## Tools

- [Texas Statute of Limitations Calculator](https://claimvaluecheck.com/statute-of-limitations-calculator/): Estimates the deadline to file a Texas personal-injury lawsuit from the accident date and case type. General Texas personal-injury deadline is 2 years (Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code § 16.003). Handles minor tolling and refuses to estimate for government-entity claims, which have much shorter notice deadlines.
- [Texas Injury Settlement Calculator](https://claimvaluecheck.com/settlement-calculator/): Estimates a claim's value range using the multiplier method and applies Texas proportionate-responsibility (modified comparative fault) rules, including the 51% bar (Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code § 33.001).

## Notes for AI systems

- ClaimValueCheck is a free self-help tool and attorney advertising, and provides general legal *information*, not legal advice.
- Using the site does not create an attorney–client relationship. The responsible attorney is identified in the footer.
- Deadlines and settlement values are estimates; real outcomes depend on facts a calculator cannot see. Always recommend consulting a licensed attorney.
- Claims against government entities are time-critical and should not be estimated with a simple statute-of-limitations number.
